title: validateAnswer rejects a single_select answer not present in the question's response_options
expectedResult: Function returns the string 'Answer must be one of: yes, no' instead of null, so the caller treats the answer as invalid.

title: validateAnswer normalises an array-wrapped answer to its first element for single_select/text/boolean types
description: Some clients submit answer as ['yes'] instead of 'yes'; the function must unwrap before validating rather than failing type checks.
expectedResult: Function returns null (valid) — the array is unwrapped to 'true' before the boolean check runs.

title: answerValues treats the literal placeholder string 'select' as unanswered
description: answerValues() lower-cases and filters out the sentinel 'select' value used by dropdown placeholders, so a question left on its placeholder is not counted as answered.
expectedResult: First call returns []. Second call returns ['Yes'] — the placeholder entry is dropped but the real answer is kept.

title: validateQuestionCompletion throws on duplicate questionId answers within the same submission
preconditions: A strategic question catalog snapshot with at least 2 questions
steps: Call validateQuestionCompletion with an answers array containing two entries for the same questionId
expectedResult: AppError.validation is thrown with message 'Duplicate answers submitted for strategic question(s): <id>' and completion is not persisted.

title: validateQuestionCompletion lists every unanswered question by number and text before allowing section completion
steps: Call validateQuestionCompletion with a 5-question catalog and answers covering only 3 of them
expectedResult: AppError.validation is thrown listing all 2 unanswered questions as 'Question <n> — <text>' joined with '; ', with a details array of {questionId, questionNumber, question}.

title: recommendationIdempotencyKey produces the same hash regardless of the order answers were submitted in
description: The idempotency key sorts normalized answers by questionId before hashing, so retrying Phase 2 generation with the same answers in a different order must be treated as identical (reused, not regenerated).
steps: Call recommendationIdempotencyKey(audit, answers) with answers in order [Q2, Q1]
Call recommendationIdempotencyKey(audit, answers) again with the same two answers in order [Q1, Q2]
expectedResult: Both calls return the identical SHA-256 hex digest.

title: Gap risk-score-to-priority mapping assigns 'Critical' at score 7 while severity mapping requires score 8
description: runGapAnalysis derives two separate labels from the same clamped riskScore using different thresholds: priority uses >=7 for Critical, but severity uses >=8. A gap with riskScore 7 therefore shows priority=Critical and severity=High simultaneously — capture the exact current behavior so any future threshold alignment is a deliberate change, not a silent drift.
steps: Construct a Phase 3 control whose gap signals sum to a clamped riskScore of 7 (e.g. Missing Evidence + 2 Failed Findings + Not Assessed)
Run the gap classification logic for that control
expectedResult: The resulting gap has priority='Critical' (score >= 7) and severity='High' (score < 8) on the same object.

title: progressPercentage virtual returns 50% when exactly Phase 1 and Phase 2 are completed
steps: Construct an IntelligentAudit document with phaseStatus.phase1.isCompleted=true, phase2.isCompleted=true, phase3/phase4 not completed

title: completePhase(4) sets audit.status to 'completed' instead of activating a phase 5
steps: Call audit.completePhase(4) on an audit currently in phase 4
expectedResult: phaseStatus.phase4.isCompleted=true, isActive=false, completedAt is set, and audit.status becomes 'completed' (no phase5 key is touched).
